explanation: Compared against Written on the Wall II (archived all.html and the definitions file wowIIdefs.js from cms.uhd.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/, via the Wayback Machine; the live site does not respond), Conjecture 172 (listed as open, Aug 8, 2005): 'If G is a simple connected graph, then L_s(G) ≥ −1 + Δ(B) + dist_min(M^2), where B is the boundary and M^2 is the set of maximum degree vertices of the second power graph of G'. Definitions: Δ(S) = maximum{deg_G(v) | v in S}; B = vertices of maximum eccentricity; dist_min(M) = minimum{dist_G(u,v) | u and v are in M} (necessarily over distinct pairs, else it would always be 0); G^2 joins vertices at distance ≤ 2. The Lean declaration is the negation of the universal statement Ls G ≥ −1 + peripheryMaxDegree G + distMin G (squareMaximumDegreeVertices G), with degrees of peripheral vertices taken in G, M^2 the maximum-degree vertices of G², and distMin the least G-distance between distinct vertices of the set (0 if fewer than two). I checked the cited counterexample D_9 (two triangles whose apexes are joined by a path with nine edges, 14 vertices) by hand: every connected dominating set contains the ten path vertices, so L_s = 14 − 10 = 4; the periphery is the four non-path triangle vertices, of degree 2; the G²-degrees are 5 at path vertices 1 and 8 and smaller elsewhere, so M^2 = {1, 8} at G-distance 7; the bound would read 4 ≥ −1 + 2 + 7 = 8. So the Lean statement is true. Interpretive caveat (hence severity 2): the source does not say whether the distance in dist_min(M^2) is measured in G or in G²; by analogy with conjectures 181–186, where invariants are evaluated on the graph G², the intended reading may be G²-distance. The Lean statement fixes G-distance, which makes the refuted inequality stronger and hence the negation logically weaker than the negation under the G² reading. This does not affect the verdict here, since D_9 also refutes the G² reading (distance ⌈7/2⌉ = 4, giving 4 ≥ 5), but the docstring does not mention the choice. Minor: the question tag is used although the source states a conjecture.
